Translated by the Imperial Subject Hōten, the Great Master Dengyō, by imperial decree.

At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra, having witnessed this rare occurrence—that a person who had committed the act of killing had gone forth under the Buddha and attained the fruit of sainthood—approached the Buddha and said:
"It is rare, World-Honored One!"
The Tathāgata, with great compassion and skillful means, proclaims the True Dharma.

For those who have committed acts of killing whose karmic roots are deep and heavy, the Tathāgata can deliver them effectively in a single instant, enabling them to attain liberation; this is the power of the skillful means of all Buddhas and Tathāgatas.

The Dharma he teaches is entirely the realm of all Buddhas; it is understood well only by the Great Being Mañjuśrī and those bodhisattvas who have donned the armor of diligence, and is not the realm of us śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas.

Why is this? Because the wisdom of the śrāvakas is narrow and inferior; they are not even able to discern the capacities and dispositions of sentient beings, so how could they possibly understand the methods of skillful means?
The Buddha said, “So it is, so it is, Śāriputra!”
The realm of all Buddhas can only be entered by Bodhisattvas who have attained the perfection of the dharmas of patience (*kṣānti*).
Although you Śrāvakas have abandoned the view of a personal entity (*pudgala-dṛṣṭi*), you seek only the Nirvāṇa of self-benefit;

and although you practice the merits of asceticism (*dhūta-guṇa*), you seek only the perfection of morality, concentration, and wisdom, rather than delighting in training in the Dharma of all Buddhas.
All that is performed possesses marks and obstructions; therefore, the realm of the Buddha cannot be conceived.
"Śāriputra, you should now know this:"

As for those who were converted and led by him to commit acts of killing, these individuals had already, in the presence of five hundred buddhas, respectfully made offerings and planted various roots of goodness, and they had also previously heard such a Dharma as this.

Therefore, this person now hears the exposition of the True Dharma before me; by the power of roots of goodness from past lives, they have come to perceive the true principle of all phenomena and are liberated in accordance with the Dharma.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

If a person hears even a single four-line verse of this true Dharma, that person shall not fall into the evil realms; they will be liberated from suffering and, with certainty, attain the all-knowledge of Buddhahood."
"How much more so for those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and practice according to the Dharma!
The merit obtained by such a person is immeasurable and boundless.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, together with the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the great śrāvakas such as Kāśyapa, and King Magadha along with his officials and retinue, all simultaneously returned to Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa to join the assembly of Śākyamuni Buddha.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s assembly, they each prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the King of Magadha, saying:
“Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva has already extensively revealed and expounded for you the rare Dharma of the Mahāyāna, which you hold dear.”
"Do you truly understand this Dharma?
The King replied,
"Venerable One!"
"I have already understood this rare and marvelous Dharma.
Śāriputra said, "In what manner have you come to understand it?"

He replied: "As it appears to me, regarding all phenomena (dharmas), one is free from all defilement and attachment; there is neither gain nor loss, neither grasping nor abandoning. It is not the domain of the mind, being without the characteristic of anything attainable—this is the true Dharma."
"By understanding it in this way, doubt is forever extinguished, and all hindrances and burdens have no source from which they can arise.
At that time, Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
This King of Magadha’s roots of goodness have matured, and he delights in the profound flavor of the Mahāyāna Dharma.
Having seen that phenomena are unarisen, he has exhausted all karmic obstructions; is this a true cessation?
Is there something further?
What is the meaning of this matter?
We pray that the Buddha will explain it for us.
The Buddha said:
“Śāriputra! All the karmic obstructions of this king have been completely extinguished; not even a trace remains.”
"Śāriputra! For example, suppose there were a mustard seed, minute in size; could Mount Sumeru, the king of mountains, crush and destroy it?
You should now know this:"
The king’s karmic obstructions are like a mustard seed, while the profound Dharma I have proclaimed is like that king of mountains.
Therefore, when this king hears the profound Dharma, how could there be any remaining obstructions that are not utterly extinguished?
Śāriputra said: "How extraordinary, World-Honored One!
This king possesses sharp faculties and clear understanding; he has been able to hear the Dharma, comprehend it, and extinguish all hindrances."
"What the Buddha has said is indeed not false.
The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!..."

This king, having in the past reverently made offerings to seventy-two koṭis of Buddhas and planted various roots of goodness, heard the True Dharma in the presence of those Buddhas; by virtue of these roots of goodness, he will certainly realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment in the future.
Furthermore, the Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"Do you see this Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva? He replied:
“I have seen it,” he replied. The Buddha said,
“This King of Magadha now has a great karmic affinity with the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.”
Śāriputra! In the past, there was an eon named Vimala, in which a Buddha appeared in the world named Subāhu.
Within that eon, three koṭis of other Buddhas also appeared in the world; all such Buddhas had their resolve for the Path awakened by the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
The lifespans of those Tathāgatas are long and far-reaching, as they turn the great wheel of Dharma to benefit sentient beings.
Within that kalpa, this King of Magadha encountered the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, who instructed and transformed him, causing him to resolve upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Once the King had resolved his mind [upon enlightenment], he planted various roots of goodness under such Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, and heard and received the rare Dharma of the Mahāyāna.
By these causes and conditions, his roots of goodness became profound and deep.
“Śāriputra! You should know this now:

after this king of Magadha has passed away, beyond four hundred buddha-fields in the upward direction, there is a buddha-field named Adorned. There, the Buddha is named Ratnaskandha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha.”

Born therein, this king also beheld the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and heard the profound Dharma; having heard it, he understood it and realized the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).

Furthermore, when the Bodhisattva Maitreya attains perfect enlightenment in this Sahā world, this King of Magadha will come from that Adorned Buddha-field to be born here; within the Dharma of the Tathāgata Maitreya, he shall become a bodhisattva named Acala, and at that time, he shall also behold the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
At that time, after the Tathāgata Maitreya had once again proclaimed for the Bodhisattva Acala the Dharma as he had heard it in the past, he addressed the assembly, saying:
"Do you see the Bodhisattva Acala?"
Is this Bodhisattva anyone else?
He is none other than the King of Magadha during the time of the Buddha Śākyamuni in the past.
Having heard and received the true Dharma from the presence of the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, he attained the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“When that Tathāgata Maitreya preached the sublime Dharma for the Bodhisattva Acala, eight thousand bodhisattvas in the assembly attained the patience regarding the non-arising of phenomena (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), and twenty-four thousand minor bodhisattvas entered the first stage (prathamā bhūmi).”

“Śāriputra! From that time forward, for eight hundred asaṃkhyeya kalpas, the Bodhisattva Acala practiced the path, purifying all Buddha-fields and teaching and transforming sentient beings so that they might proceed to the stages of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and bodhisattvas. He caused all sentient beings to extinguish all hindrances, to understand and awaken to the true Dharma, and to give rise to no further doubt or confusion.”

"After those eight hundred *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas have passed, that Bodhisattva Acala shall realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the world-system called Vimalā; he shall be known as the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Pure Realm, fully endowed with the ten titles."

The lifespan of that Buddha will be four intermediate kalpas, and his True Dharma shall remain in the world for one koṭi of years. There will be a community of seven hundred thousand śrāvakas, all fully endowed with the three types of supernormal knowledge (traividyā) and the six higher faculties (ṣaḍabhijñā), having attained the eight liberations (aṣṭavimokṣa). There will also be a community of twelve koṭis of great bodhisattvas, all fully endowed with wisdom and skillful means. All sentient beings in that land will take delight in the profoundly deep Dharma.

That Buddha, the Tathāgata, extensively proclaimed and expounded this for them; and the sentient beings, having heard the Dharma and attained awakening and understanding, were freed from all afflictions, their bodies and minds became pure, and each of them no longer gave rise to the notion of a self-view.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha spoke to Śāriputra concerning the matter of the King of Magadha attaining Buddhahood.
At that moment, thirty-two thousand devaputras within the assembly resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and all made this vow:
"May we be born in that world of Non-defilement, and may we behold that Tathāgata of Pure Realm as he realizes the path of perfect enlightenment."
Śākyamuni Buddha then gave them this prediction:
"You shall all be born in that world and behold that Tathāgata as he attains the path of perfect enlightenment."
At that time, King Magadha had a crown prince named Candrasvāti, who was eight years of age; he had previously accompanied his father, the king, to the assembly of the Buddha.
Having heard the teaching of the Dharma, he immediately untied the pearl necklace from his own neck and offered it to the Buddha, making this aspiration:

"By means of these roots of goodness from my present offering to the Buddha, I dedicate them toward Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi; may I, in a future life, be born in that pure realm within the Tathāgata’s land as a Golden Wheel-Turning King."
Until the end of my life, I shall provide those four requisites as offerings to that Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus.
After that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, I shall collect his relics and venerate them with respectful offerings.
"May I, in succession, realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment (*anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*) in that very realm.

At that time, after Prince Candrasrihad had made this vow, through the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, the offered necklace remained suspended in mid-air; above that Buddha, it transformed into a pavilion made of the seven precious gems, within which was a seat of the seven precious gems, upon which sat a Buddha in the full-lotus posture (*paryaṅka*), endowed with all the marks and signs of perfection and adorned in every way.

At that time, the World-Honored One emitted rays of light of various colors from his face—namely blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, purple, azure, and green. These lights shone universally throughout boundless worlds, reaching upward as far as the Brahma world; the radiance was so brilliant that it eclipsed the sun and moon, causing them both to disappear.
The light returned once more, circled the Buddha three times, and entered through the crown of the head of the World-Honored One.
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, and with palms joined toward the Buddha, spoke these verses:
"The Great Muni who has reached the further shore, Endowed with all supreme merits..."
Honored by the world of devas and humans alike, the All-Knowing One is free from all attachments.
The mental activities and faculties of sentient beings, the Tathāgata knows each and every one;
he proclaims the sublime Dharma to benefit all living beings, becoming the most supreme in all the worlds.
The rare and great radiance you emit Universally illuminates all lands in the ten directions;
Koti-nayuta sentient beings Who are touched by this light attain peace and security.
The Sugata has fully perfected the ten powers; with mindfulness and wisdom complete, he transcends the world.
He skillfully discerns the mental activities of sentient beings; in preaching the Dharma to sever doubts, there is none equal to him.
All the Brahma Kings and Śakras, the sun, moon, stars, and all the devas,
having heard the Buddha proclaim this wondrous Dharma-gate, were freed from all afflictions and attained peace and stability.
The Tathāgata is the most honored among all assemblies; he resolves all the doubts of sentient beings.
For what reason does he emit this light today?
I pray that the Buddha, out of his great compassion, will explain it to me.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Do you see this Prince Candraketu?
Ānanda replied to the Buddha:
“Yes, indeed, I have seen it,” [he replied]. The Buddha said, “Ānanda!
In past lives, this prince has already cultivated the practices of a bodhisattva and made offerings to me, deeply planting roots of goodness.
Because these conditions have now reached maturity, he has today before me resolved his mind upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and given rise to great vows.
For this reason, he has emitted this radiance.

"Ānanda! This prince shall, in the future, be born into the Dharma of the Tathāgata Viśuddhaviṣaya (Pure Realm) in the world Anupalipta (Untainted) as a Cakravartin King of Gold, and shall make offerings to that Buddha and the assembly of bhikṣus."
After that Buddha has passed into parinirvāṇa, they shall collect his relics and reverently make offerings to them.

When this person’s life there comes to an end, they will be reborn in Tuṣita Heaven; after a full kalpa has elapsed, they will be born in the world named Unstained (Vimalā), where they will realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment, becoming a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Sūryaketu, fully endowed with the ten titles.
"The lifespan of that Buddha, the World-Honored One, as well as that of his assembly of Bodhisattvas and Śrāvakas, is entirely equal.
At that time, the multitude of Bodhisattvas who had gathered from other directions, having heard the prediction bestowed upon Prince Candrasri, addressed the Buddha together, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Now, Śākyamuni Buddha and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva perform great buddha-work in all directions and places, benefiting sentient beings without fail.

Why is this? Because the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, out of great compassion, employ various skillful means to teach and transform sentient beings in every location—from royal capitals and cities to towns and even villages—enabling those beings to hear the Dharma and attain liberation, to be free from all fears, and to sever all heavy obstacles of affliction.

Today we have attained the opportunity to hear the sublime Dharma expounded by the Buddha and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī upon this very ground, and to witness this rare occurrence of the emission of light; it shall truly not have been in vain, as it brings benefit to sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bodhisattvas, saying: "Good sons! It is so, it is so."

If a Buddha or a Bodhisattva preaches the True Dharma and performs Buddha-works in various places for the sake of sentient beings, one should regard those places as being like Buddha-stūpas and shrines.

Why is this? Because in a past life, when I encountered the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara, out of a mind of faith and reverence, I spread my hair upon the ground to receive the feet of that Buddha, and at that time I attained the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
That Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara, knowing that I had attained the perfection of the dharma of patience, immediately bestowed upon me the prediction of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, speaking these words:
"In a future age, after incalculable eons (*asaṃkhyeya-kalpa*), you shall become a Buddha, named Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, fully endowed with the ten titles."
After that Buddha Dīpaṃkara had bestowed the prediction upon me, he addressed the assembly of bhikṣus, saying:
"You should conceive a sense of reverence for this spot; do not give rise to contempt or disdain."

Why is this? Because in this place there was a son of good family who spread his hair upon the ground to receive the World-Honored One’s feet; by virtue of that supreme power, he immediately attained the perfection of the Dharma of Patience (kṣānti).
"Therefore, all devas and humans shall regard this ground with the same veneration as they would a Buddha’s stupa or temple, no differently.
When the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara spoke these words, eighty koṭis of devas and humans, with one voice and in unison, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"We now regard this place with reverence, as if it were a stupa or temple of the Buddha.
At that time, there was an elder named Bhadradatta who, being present in that assembly, addressed Dīpaṃkara Buddha, saying:
"I shall now construct a stupa of the seven precious jewels here, so that all sentient beings may obtain merit by beholding and paying homage to it."

Then that elder, acting according to those words, gave rise to a rare and wondrous mind; he gathered various precious treasures and erected a stūpa, lofty, vast, and exquisite, adorned with all manner of ornaments, its craftsmanship so magnificent that it was completed in no time.
At that time, having completed the construction of the stupa, the elder went to the place where Dīpaṃkara Buddha was and said to him:
"World-Honored One!
I have already erected this wondrous stupa made of the seven precious substances; how much merit shall I obtain in a future age?"
The Buddha said: "Householder!

If there were a son of good family who were to take soil from the ground up to the water’s edge at the site where a bodhisattva mahāsattva has realized the stage of the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti), and were to hold and reverently make offerings of this soil, the mass of merit obtained would still be equal to making offerings to the stūpas and temples of all Buddhas, without any difference; how much more so for you now, having given rise to pure faith and constructed a stūpa of the seven treasures?"
"The mass of merit you have acquired is many times greater than before—immeasurable, boundless, and beyond comparison.
At that time, the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara further addressed the elder Bhadradatta, saying:
"You have now planted deep roots of goodness here; in a future age, you shall receive from Śākyamuni Buddha the prophecy of your attainment of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha, for the sake of the great bodhisattvas who had gathered from other directions, spoke of the causes and conditions of his past receiving of the prediction.
He further addressed the bodhisattvas, saying:
"You should now know:
In the past, having planted roots of goodness in the presence of Dīpaṃkara Buddha, I have now attained Buddhahood.
At that time, when I attained the stage of the dharma of patience (kṣānti), those gods and humans revered me as if I were a stūpa;
you all should likewise conceive a thought of reverence toward this ground today.
"Furthermore, O Bodhisattvas! You should know this:
who else could that householder Bhadradatta have been at that time? It was none other than you."
This is none other than the present Elder Bhadrika.
In that Dharma, he was also named Bhadrika; in a future age, this person shall attain Buddhahood, known by the name Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Suprabha, fully endowed with the ten titles.
"Furthermore, O Bodhisattvas!

Regarding this profound Dharma which I have taught, if there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who are able to hear, receive, read, recite, and expound it to others, the place where such persons dwell will be gazed upon with reverence by devas and humans, no different from a stūpa or temple of the Buddha."
"Furthermore, O Bodhisattvas!

If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who practice the perfection of giving, and they gather the seven precious jewels to fill a trichiliocosm, making offerings to the Buddhas and the assembly of bhikṣus six times throughout the day and night, continuing in this manner until the end of the kalpa—it would not equal the merit obtained by one who hears, receives, reads, and recites even a single four-line verse of this unprecedented True Dharma; the latter's merit is many times superior to the former."

"Furthermore, if a person practices the path of precepts and maintains the Buddha's disciplinary teachings for an entire kalpa without any transgression, thereby perfecting all the merits of pure morality;
this does not equal the merit of listening to, receiving, reading, and reciting this True Dharma. Compared to the former, the latter merit exceeds it by a factor of a thousand."

"Furthermore, if a person practices the conduct of patience (*kṣānti-caryā*), constantly practicing forbearance throughout an entire eon and never giving rise to anger or malice toward any sentient being, they may thereby achieve perfection in the conduct of patience;

yet this does not equal the merit of obtaining the full realization of Dharma-patience (*dharma-kṣānti*) by hearing, receiving, reading, reciting, and practicing according to the Dharma within this True Dharma—this latter way is supreme."

"Furthermore, if a person cultivates diligence by zealously teaching and transforming all sentient beings throughout an entire kalpa without ever giving rise to a mind of indolence, they will thereby attain the perfection of diligence;
yet the merit obtained from hearing, receiving, reading, and reciting this True Dharma is many times greater than that."

"Furthermore, if there were a person who cultivates meditative concentration and dwells in samādhi for an entire kalpa, focusing the mind with one-pointed attention and free from all distraction, thereby attaining perfection in the practice of concentration;
this would not equal the merit obtained by listening to, receiving, reading, and reciting this True Dharma, which is many times superior to the former."
Furthermore, if a person cultivates wisdom by practicing various wisdom-expedients throughout an entire kalpa and thereby attains the perfection of wisdom,
it would not equal the merit obtained from hearing, receiving, reading, and reciting this True Dharma, which is vast and immeasurable, and can swiftly bring to fulfillment the fruit of all-knowledge.
At that time, the great bodhisattvas who had gathered from other directions, having heard Śākyamuni Buddha proclaim the profound merits of this Dharma, each addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Having heard and received this Dharma, we shall return to our own lands to expound it for others, proclaiming and disseminating it so that all sentient beings may each obtain benefit.
Śākyamuni Buddha said: “Excellent, excellent,
sons of good family!
"You all should proclaim this Dharma and extensively perform the Buddha-work for the sake of sentient beings.
At that time, the bodhisattvas who had gathered scattered exquisite flowers, filling the trichiliocosm, as an offering to Śākyamuni Buddha and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, and spoke these words:
"May this True Dharma long abide within Jambudvīpa to benefit all sentient beings."
We pray that Śākyamuni Buddha and Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva may long abide in this world, emitting the light of the Dharma to illumine all sentient beings.

That we have now been able to enter this assembly to behold the Buddha, the World-Honored One, and hear the preaching of the sublime Dharma, is entirely due to the exhortation of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
"Even if we were to sacrifice our heads, eyes, hands, and feet to offer them as gifts, we still could not repay the Bodhisattva’s kindness;
even this scattering of flowers does not yet constitute an offering that repays his grace."

Therefore, if there are good sons or good daughters who have the opportunity to see the Buddhas and hear the True Dharma, even if they were to sacrifice their heads, eyes, hands, and feet, they could never repay the kindness of the Buddhas.

Therefore, you must give rise to pure faith toward the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and all the sutras and teachings; you should honor and make offerings to them, and never harbor thoughts of contempt or doubt—those who conceive such thoughts will incur grave and heavy offenses.

At that time, after those great bodhisattvas who had come from other directions had spoken these words, they prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, circumambulated him three times to the right, and immediately vanished from within the assembly. They returned to their respective buddha-fields and, each standing before their own Buddha, spoke as follows:

"In the Sahā world, we heard the Śākyamuni Buddha and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī proclaiming the True Dharma; we have already received and upheld it, and now declare it here for the sake of sentient beings, so that all sentient beings may decisively realize *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*."
At that time, the Venerable Mahākāśyapa addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This True Dharma is truly rare.”

As I have seen: when the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī accepted a meal offering within the royal palace of Magadha and the Bodhisattva expounded this Dharma for the king, the king at that time realized the patience of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
I, too, rejoice in hearing and receiving this Dharma; I reproach myself deeply and give rise to great joy.
World-Honored One!

In the future final age, if there are sentient beings who hear this true Dharma and give rise to right understanding, such persons will be able to know the self-nature of dharmas, sever all doubts, and will certainly attain equal and perfect enlightenment in the future.
The Buddha said:
“Kāśyapa, excellent, excellent! You have spoken these words well.”
"If all sentient beings hear this Dharma, they shall certainly realize the fruit of Buddha-enlightenment in the future.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva, saying:

"You should now receive and uphold this Dharma; in the future final age, proclaim and expound it for the sake of all sentient beings, so that all sentient beings may obtain benefit and attain great happiness."
The Bodhisattva Maitreya addressed the Buddha, saying:
“As the World-Honored One has commanded, I shall receive and uphold it.
World-Honored One!”
In the past, I also heard and received this Dharma from former Buddhas; now, before the Buddha, I have heard it once again, for which I am deeply grateful and fortunate.
In the future, I shall protect, assist, proclaim, and disseminate it, ensuring that the Dharma endures for a long time.

Until the end of this life, I shall be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven; and if among those in that heaven there are any whose faculties are mature and who delight in the Mahāyāna, I shall likewise reveal and expound it for them, causing them to resolve upon the Way, so that [the teaching] shall not be severed in Jambudvīpa to the south.

Furthermore, in the final age, if there are men or women who receive, uphold, read, and recite this True Dharma, and if they are harassed and disturbed by various māras, I shall at that time secretly go among them to provide protection and assistance, ensuring that the hosts of māras find no opportunity against them.
Furthermore, World-Honored One!

In the final age, if there should be those who hear this Dharma and listen to it, receive it, read it, recite it, and practice it according to the Dharma, you should know that these are established by the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha.
At that time, the Buddha addressed Śakra, Lord of the Devas, saying:
"Kauśika! You should now receive, uphold, and keep in mind this True Dharma of mine, so as to provide protection and assistance during the final age hereafter."
Why is this? Because this Dharma can sever all doubts, purify all karmic obstructions, is equal to all dharmas, and furthermore possesses great majestic power.
Śakra, you should know:
when you engage in battle with those asuras, you should keep this teaching in mind; at that time, you shall be victorious and they shall be defeated and retreat.

Furthermore, if a person encounters difficulties such as those caused by kings, bandits, tigers, wolves, insects, beasts, or evil people, and is able to contemplate and keep this Dharma in mind, that person shall immediately be freed from all such perils.
Then Śakra, Lord of the Devas, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"As the World-Honored One has commanded, I shall protect and uphold it.

In the future, at the end of the age, wherever there may be a place—be it a kingdom, city, district, town, or even a village—where this Dharma exists, I shall go there to pay respect and make offerings."
"If there be those who uphold this Dharma, I shall protect and assist them.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"You must now receive and uphold this True Dharma of mine, and in the future final age, proclaim and expound it for the sake of all sentient beings."
Why is this? Because this Dharma is exceedingly profound and has never existed before.
If any man or woman upholds this Dharma, they shall be freed from all doubts and delusions, and shall extinguish all afflictions, transgressions, and defilements.
"Therefore, you should remember and uphold this.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Empowered by the Buddha's spiritual authority, I shall proclaim this Dharma in the final age so that all sentient beings may obtain benefit.
World-Honored One!"
"What is the name of this sutra?
How should we receive and uphold it?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“This sutra is titled ‘The Unprecedented True Dharma’; it should be upheld in this manner.

At that time, having entrusted [the teaching] to the bodhisattvas, the śrāvakas, and Śakra, the World-Honored One immediately emitted a great radiance from the left and right sides of his body within the assembly, universally illuminating all worlds throughout the ten directions.
From within that light, a subtle and wondrous sound issued forth, universally proclaiming to the great assembly:

"The True Dharma taught by the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha shall remain undestroyed until the kalpa ends and the great ocean dries up; it will continue to bring great benefit to sentient beings."
At that moment, after the sound had been emitted, the radiance released returned to the Buddha’s body.
Then the World-Honored One again addressed Ānanda, saying:

“Uphold these words of the Buddha; be careful not to forget them. In the future final age, you shall proclaim and disseminate this Dharma, extensively bringing benefit, peace, and joy to all sentient beings.”
When Śākyamuni Buddha spoke this unprecedented True Dharma, ninety-six thousand devas and humans were distanced from and freed of dust and defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye;
seven hundred and eighty thousand people resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*;
and thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas attained the patience regarding the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
Eighty thousand bhikṣus, not grasping at any phenomena, attained the exhaustion of outflows and the liberation of mind.

At that moment, the trichiliocosm shook in six ways, and the devas of the desire and form realms played hundreds of thousands of celestial musical instruments in the sky to make offerings to the World-Honored One and the Dharma he taught.

When Śākyamuni Buddha preached this True Dharma, all the celestial Māras and followers of external paths were struck with terror upon hearing it and all took refuge in the Buddha—just as when the Buddha first turned the Wheel of Dharma and subdued the celestial Māras; today was no different.
"This Dharma is the seal of all Buddhas, the Great Dharma Seal, and the Seal of Liberation; all those who possess wisdom should train in this way and practice accordingly."

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, King Magadha and his retinue, Mañjuśrī and the other great Bodhisattvas, Mahākāśyapa, Ānanda, Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, and the other great Śrāvakas, as well as the entire assembly—including gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas of the world—having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly delighted; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Unprecedented True Dharma, Scroll Six.
